mainTopic: The left-hand קומץ and קדושה בכלי, burning the קומץ in parts, when its burning permits the שיריים, and placing offerings on the wood pile
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about a כהן who moved the קומץ into his left hand. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון let him move it back to the right hand. The חכמים say the left hand ruins it for good, because the קומץ needs קדושה בכלי. From this the גמרא shows that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון do not require a כלי, which refutes רב נחמן. Next, רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן argue over whether the קומץ may be burned in only two parts or in many, and רבי זירא ties their argument to minimum sizes. Then רבי חנינא and רבי יוחנן argue over when the burning of the קומץ permits the כהנים to eat the שיריים. A ברייתא about items burned at sunset is used to challenge רבי יוחנן, and the גמרא answers that the מזבח 'taking hold' of the קומץ is different from permitting the שיריים. The amud ends with questions about placing the קומץ or the limbs under or beside the wood pile, and the last question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A bad thought while the handful is in the left hand
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that if the כהן had a thought of eating outside its place or beyond its time while the handful was in his left hand, the offering is פסול but carries no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had in mind, about it, either outside its place or beyond its time, it is invalid, but there is no כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא from the previous page about a כהן who put the קמיצה into his left hand. Here it rules what happens if he had a wrong thought while it was there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a thought of 'beyond its time' makes an offering פיגול, which carries כרת. Here it only makes the offering פסול, with no כרת. Holding the handful in the left hand is not a proper עבודה, so the thought cannot create פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: He had in mind, meaning a thought during the service about eating or offering improperly
Outside its proper place
Beyond its proper time
Invalid or disqualified
Spiritual 'cutting off', the punishment for eating פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume every 'beyond its time' thought creates פיגול. It only does so when the service itself is done properly, and holding the handful in the left hand is not proper service.

phrases.english: And he had in mind, about it,
phrases.notes: The case began on the previous page: the כהן put the handful in his left hand, and while it was there he had this thought.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ בֵּין חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ –
phrases.english: whether outside its place or beyond its time –
it is invalid, but there is no karet for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחִישֵּׁב עָלֶיהָ בֵּין חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ בֵּין חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bad thought made while the handful is in the left hand makes the offering פסול but brings no כרת.

steps.title: Another version: a thought while the handful is in the right hand
steps.stepSummary: In another version of the ברייתא, a thought made while the handful is in the right hand works normally: outside its place makes it פסול, and beyond its time makes it פיגול with כרת. This is the view of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had in mind, about it, outside its place, it is invalid, with no כרת. If beyond its time, it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it. These are the words of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the ברייתא. In this version the thought happens once the handful is back in the right hand, and the normal rules of פיגול apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the handful has been returned to the right hand, the service counts as proper. So a 'beyond its time' thought creates real פיגול with כרת. This shows that for רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, putting the handful in the left hand did not permanently ruin it.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made disgusting by a thought of eating it beyond its time
One is liable to כרת for eating it

phrases.english: [Another version:] If he had in mind, about it, outside its place –
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the standard גמרא, but the corrected wording leaves it out. Read this line as another version of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: it is invalid, but there is no karet for it.
If beyond its time – it is piggul,
and one is liable to karet for it,
these are the words of Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, once the handful is back in the right hand, a 'beyond its time' thought creates פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: The חכמים: putting it in the left hand ruins it
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue: as soon as the handful was put in the left hand, that act alone disqualified it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: once he put it in the left hand, its placing there has disqualified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposing view of the חכמים. For them, there is no fixing the handful by moving it back to the right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון let the כהן move the handful back to his right hand. The חכמים say the moment it touched the left hand, it became permanently פסול. The גמרא will now ask for the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The left hand, which is not valid for עבודה
Its placing disqualified it
Once, as soon as

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Once he put it in the left hand –
its placing there has disqualified it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the disputing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, putting the קמיצה in the left hand disqualifies it permanently.

steps.title: Asking for the חכמים' reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the left hand ruins the handful for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for the logic behind the חכמים so it can explain it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why can't the handful simply go back to the right hand? The answer will show what the dispute is really about.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים hold that the left hand disqualifies the handful permanently.

steps.title: It needs a כלי, so the left hand is like spilled blood
steps.stepSummary: The קמיצה must be made holy in a כלי שרת. Putting it in the left hand is like blood that spilled from the animal's neck onto the floor and was gathered up afterward, which is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it needs to be made holy in a vessel. Once he put it in the left hand, it becomes like blood that spilled from the animal's neck onto the floor and was then gathered up, which is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the חכמים: the handful must go into a כלי שרת to become holy. Before that happens, the left hand counts like the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood that falls on the floor before it reaches a כלי is ruined, and gathering it up later does not help. In the same way, the handful went somewhere improper before it was put in a כלי, so moving it back does not help. The reason rests on one idea: the need for קדושה בכלי.

keyTerms.meaning: Being made holy by placing it in a כלי שרת (service vessel)
The animal's neck, where the blood comes out at שחיטה
The floor
He gathered it up

steps.whyThisMatters: This reason sets up the inference in the next step: if the חכמים need a כלי, then רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון apparently do not.

phrases.english: Because it requires sanctification in a vessel,
and once he put it in the left hand –
it becomes like blood that spilled
from an animal's neck onto the floor
and he gathered it up, which is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים require קדושה בכלי, so the left hand is like spilled blood that can no longer be fixed.

steps.title: Inference against רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: Since the חכמים' reason is the need for a כלי, it follows that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון do not require a כלי. This refutes רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון do not require placing it in a vessel. This is a refutation of רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the dispute: the side that lets you fix the handful must not need a כלי. That contradicts רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף, רב נחמן said that even רבי שמעון requires the handful to be made holy in a כלי. But here רבי שמעון disagrees with the חכמים, whose whole reason is the need for a כלי. So רבי שמעון must not require one, and רב נחמן's claim is attacked.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, it follows that
Placing it in a כלי שרת
A refutation that cannot be answered

phrases.english: By implication, Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon
do not require placing it in a vessel,
this is a refutation of Rav Naḥman,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא בָּעוּ מַתַּן כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from step 5 to infer the view of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that רבי שמעון requires קדושה בכלי for the קמיצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים disqualify the handful only because they require a כלי. רבי שמעון disagrees with them, so he must not require a כלי.

steps.title: The refutation stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms that רב נחמן is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion: there is no answer, so רב נחמן's view is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the word תיובתא means the challenge stands and no defense is offered. The conclusion is that רבי שמעון does not require the handful to be made holy in a כלי.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים say the left hand ruins the קמיצה because it needs קדושה בכלי. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון let it go back to the right hand, which shows they do not require a כלי. That refutes רב נחמן.

phrases.english: It is a conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the refutation raised in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן is refuted: according to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, the קמיצה does not need to be made holy in a כלי שרת.

steps.title: This supports רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: The ruling that, for רבי שמעון, the קומץ goes back to the right hand supports רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ruling just quoted, that the קומץ is moved back to the right hand, backs up what רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא said. This also sets up the next question about רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא held that for רבי שמעון the מנחה service must be done with the right hand. A ruling that requires moving the קומץ back to the right hand fits his view exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports him; it is a backing for his view
The son of

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Chiyya,
phrases.notes: He is the one who said that for רבי שמעון the service must be done with the right hand.

phrases.english: it supports him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא מְסַיְּיעָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב נחמן was refuted, the גמרא draws a further point from the right-hand ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא's view that for רבי שמעון the service is done with the right hand
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that for רבי שמעון the קומץ is moved back to the right hand

steps.title: Is this a refutation of רבי ינאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the same ruling refutes רבי ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that this is a refutation of רבי ינאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks if the right-hand ruling disproves רבי ינאי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי held that once the קומץ has been taken out of the כלי שרת, it may be offered in any manner. If the קומץ must be moved back to the right hand, that seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? A way of suggesting a conclusion that may later be pushed away
A refutation; a strong proof against a view

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yannai,
shall we say it is a refutation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same source that supports one אמורא now seems to attack another.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's view that after the קומץ leaves the כלי it may be offered in any manner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Requiring a return to the right hand shows that the manner still matters, which goes against רבי ינאי.

steps.title: רבי ינאי follows the תנא of הקטר, read simply
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that he follows the תנא of הקטר. That תנא allows either hand, and his words should not be split into separate cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי can say to you: I ruled like the תנא who taught about burning, and he is not teaching in separate categories.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי defends himself. He says his ruling follows a different תנא, the one who taught about הקטר, burning on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, that תנא's teaching was split into separate cases (לצדדים) to make it fit רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא. רבי ינאי reads it simply instead: burning may be done with either hand. So the right-hand ruling does not refute him. He simply follows another תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you; a defense given on someone's behalf
Burning of an offering on the מזבח
In separate categories; reading a list as different rules for different items

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ינאי is not saying the right-hand ruling is wrong. He is saying it reflects a different תנא's view, and he follows the תנא of הקטר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai can say to you:
I said my ruling according to the tanna of "burning,"
phrases.notes: This is the teaching that burning on the מזבח may be done with either the right or the left hand.

phrases.english: and he is not teaching it in separate categories.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי ינאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Following a different תנא, with a simple reading of that תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The right-hand ruling disproves רבי ינאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ינאי follows the תנא of הקטר, read plainly as allowing either hand, so he is not refuted.

steps.title: משנה: burning the handful in two parts is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the כהן burned the קומץ in two parts, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he burned its קומץ in two times, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה about burning the קומץ in two parts, to set up the dispute that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that the קומץ does not have to be burned all at once. Burning it in two parts is still כשר. The next question is how far this rule goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Its handful; the portion of the מנחה taken out and burned on the מזבח
Twice; here, in two parts
Valid; the offering is acceptable

phrases.english: If he burned its handful in two times, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section; the גמרא returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning the קומץ in two parts is כשר.

steps.title: Only two parts, or even many parts?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the rule allows only two parts. רבי יוחנן says even many parts are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: two times, but not many times. רבי יוחנן said: two times, and even many times.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים disagree about how to read the משנה's word פעמים, "twice."
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads "twice" as an exact limit: two parts are fine, but more is not. רבי יוחנן reads "twice" as just an example: burning the קומץ in many small parts is also כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Many times; burning in many small parts

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
"Twice" — but not many times,
and Rabbi Yochanan said:
"Twice" — and even many times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי פַּעֲמַיִם וְלֹא פַּעֲמֵי פַעֲמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the משנה's word "twice" goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע בן לוי allows only two parts; רבי יוחנן allows even many parts.

steps.title: What is the real difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind the disagreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what principle these two אמוראים really disagree about. This sets up רבי זירא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know the underlying idea that makes one say "only two" and the other "even many."

keyTerms.meaning: What is between them? What is the practical or conceptual difference?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the dispute just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the dispute of רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן

steps.title: רבי זירא: the size of the handful and of each burning
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says they disagree about two questions. First, does a קומץ smaller than two olives count? Second, does burning less than a כזית count?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: whether there can be a קומץ less than two olives, and whether there can be a burning less than an olive-bulk, is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question. The dispute is about minimum sizes: the size of the whole קומץ, and the size of each separate burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both questions ask whether amounts smaller than certain measures still count. One is a קומץ smaller than two olives. The other is a burning of less than a כזית. These size questions are what lie behind "only twice" versus "even many times."

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour taken from a מנחה
Two olive-sizes
An act of burning on the מזבח
An olive-bulk; a basic halachic measure

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה allows burning the קומץ in two parts. רבי יהושע בן לוי allows only two, and רבי יוחנן allows even many. According to רבי זירא, the dispute depends on whether a קומץ smaller than two olives counts, and whether burning less than a כזית counts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
whether there is a handful less than two olives,
and whether there is a burning less than an olive-bulk —
that is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא יֵשׁ קוֹמֶץ פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנֵי זֵיתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the dispute is based on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether a קומץ smaller than two olives counts, and whether burning less than a כזית counts.

steps.title: How each אמורא fits into the two questions
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that a קומץ must be at least two olives and that a burning must be at least a כזית. רבי יוחנן holds that neither minimum applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds: a קומץ is not less than two olives, and a burning is not less than a כזית. רבי יוחנן holds: a קומץ can be less than two olives, and a burning can be less than a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי זירא's answer. It tells us which side of each of the two questions each אמורא takes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהושע בן לוי says a קומץ is at least two olives and each burning must be at least a כזית, the קומץ can only be split into two parts. רבי יוחנן sets no minimum for either one, so the קומץ may be burned in many small parts.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the קומץ is at least two olives and each burning is at least a כזית, so only two parts are allowed. רבי יוחנן: neither minimum applies, so many parts are allowed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi holds:
there is no handful less than two olives,
and there is no burning less than an olive-size.
And Rabbi Yochanan holds:
there is a handful less than two olives,
and there is a burning less than an olive-size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי זירא's answer by placing each אמורא on one side of the two questions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע בן לוי requires both minimums, so only two parts. רבי יוחנן requires neither, so many parts.

steps.title: When does the קומץ permit the leftover flour to be eaten
steps.stepSummary: A new dispute: רבי חנינא says the שיריים become permitted once the fire catches the קומץ. רבי יוחנן says only once the fire has taken hold of most of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: from when does the קומץ permit the leftovers to be eaten? רבי חנינא says: from when the fire catches it. רבי יוחנן says: from when the fire has taken hold of most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a dispute between אמוראים. The question is at what point the burning of the קומץ lets the כהנים eat the rest of the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that burning the קומץ is what permits the שיריים. The argument is only about timing. For רבי חנינא, it is enough that the fire has caught. For רבי יוחנן, most of the קומץ must already be burning.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover flour of the מנחה, eaten by the כהנים
Permits; makes something allowed
From when the fire takes hold of it (catches it)
In most of it

phrases.english: It was stated:
From when does the handful permit the remainder to be eaten?
Rabbi Chanina says:
From when the fire catches it,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
From when the fire takes hold of most of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: קוֹמֶץ מֵאֵימָתַי מַתִּיר שִׁירַיִם בַּאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It is still about burning the קומץ, but now the question is when the burning takes effect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא: once the fire catches the קומץ. רבי יוחנן: once the fire has taken hold of most of it.

steps.title: The furnace פסוק as רבי יוחנן's source
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains רבי יוחנן's reasoning from the פסוק about smoke rising like a furnace. A furnace only gives off smoke once most of it is burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to רבה בר רב יצחק: I will explain רבי יוחנן's reason to you. The פסוק says, 'and behold, the smoke of the land went up like the smoke of a furnace.' A furnace does not give off smoke until the fire has taken hold of most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a source from a פסוק for רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burning of the קומץ is described in terms of smoke, and a real furnace only makes smoke once most of it has caught fire. So the קומץ only counts as burned, and only permits the שיריים, once the fire has taken hold of most of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Smoke
A furnace or kiln
The reason
I will explain it to you

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן requires the fire to take hold of most of the קומץ, learned from 'smoke like a furnace', because a furnace only smokes once most of it is burning.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַבָּה בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to Rabba bar Rav Yitzchak:
I will explain to you the reason of Rabbi Yochanan,
the verse says:
"And behold, the smoke of the land went up
like the smoke of a furnace,"
a furnace does not give off smoke
until the fire takes hold of most of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a source from a פסוק for רבי יוחנן's side of the dispute in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that the fire must take hold of most of the קומץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 19:28: 'like the smoke of a furnace.' A furnace smokes only when most of it is burning.

steps.title: A ברייתא about offerings burned through the night
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב אדא tells רבא a ברייתא that his students quote in the name of רב עמרם. It is about limbs and fats that are put on the מזבח after sunset and burn all night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא said to רבא: your students say in the name of רב עמרם that a ברייתא teaches: I only know about things that are normally offered at night, like limbs and fats. These are brought up and burned from sunset, and they keep burning all night.
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next discussion. רבין בר רב אדא begins quoting a ברייתא to רבא, and the ברייתא keeps going after this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens with 'I only know...', which means it is first stating the case it is sure about. That case is limbs and fats of a קרבן, which may be put on the מזבח after sunset and burn through the night. We should expect the ברייתא to go on and ask about other items.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only know...': the opening of a limited rule that is about to be extended
The limbs of a קרבן
The fats of a קרבן
From sunset
Are consumed (by the fire)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda said to Rava:
Your students say that Rav Amram said,
it is taught in a baraita:
I have only items
phrases.notes: In other words: 'this much I know for sure.' The ברייתא is about to ask about other cases.

phrases.english: whose usual way is to be offered at night,
such as limbs and fats,
that one brings them up and burns them from sunset,
and they keep being consumed the whole entire night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא לְרָבָא: אָמְרִי תַּלְמִידֶיךָ אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם, תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבין בר רב אדא brings a ברייתא that will be used to challenge רבי יוחנן's rule from step 16 (that the fire must take hold of most of the קומץ). The challenge itself comes in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items normally offered at night, like limbs and fats, may be put on the מזבח after sunset and burn through the whole night.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks about burning daytime items after sunset
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. It asks how we know that items normally offered by day, like the קומץ, the לבונה and the קטורת, may be brought up and burned after sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: Things that are normally offered during the day, like the קומץ, the frankincense, the incense, the meal offering of כהנים, the meal offering of the כהן גדול, and the meal offering that goes with the נסכים: from where do we know that the כהן may bring them up and burn them after sunset?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from step 18. Now the ברייתא moves from the limbs and fats to the daytime items, and asks about burning them after sunset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 dealt with limbs and fats that burn all night. Now the ברייתא lists items whose whole service is supposed to happen by day. Its question, read literally, sounds like it allows starting them after sunset. That literal reading sets up the problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, burned together with many מנחות
The incense offering
A meal offering brought by a כהן, which is burned completely
The anointed כהן, meaning the כהן גדול
The meal offering that goes along with the wine libations

phrases.english: Items whose usual way is to be offered during the day,
for example: the handful, the frankincense, and the incense,
the meal offering of priests, the meal offering of the anointed priest,
and the meal offering of the libations,
[from where do we know] that one may bring them up and burn them after sunset?
phrases.notes: The words 'from where do we know' are not written here, but the ברייתא assumes them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 18, moving to daytime items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא assumes that daytime items may somehow be burned in connection with sunset, and it asks for the source.

steps.title: Daytime items cannot be offered after sunset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the ברייתא itself said these items are offered by day, so how can it allow starting them after sunset?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you yourself said that these are things whose way is to be offered during the day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא interrupts the ברייתא with a challenge. The ברייתא seems to contradict its own opening words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls these items 'offered by day,' but then asks how we know they may be burned after sunset. These two parts cannot both be true. The ברייתא cannot mean that the service begins at night.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But you said.' This points out a contradiction inside the same source
Their usual way, their normal procedure

phrases.english: But didn't you say their way is to be offered during the day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'מבוא השמש' (after sunset) in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Items whose service is by day cannot be started after sunset. So the ברייתא contradicts itself.

steps.title: Reread: placed at sunset and burning through the night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. It is not about starting at night. It is about items placed on the fire right at sunset that keep burning all night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא means: from where do we know that items put up together with sunset, which keep burning all through the night, are fine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing how we read the ברייתא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'after sunset' are read as 'with sunset.' The service is done while it is still day, at the very last moment. Most of the burning then happens at night. The new question is whether that night burning is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Together with sunset, at the very moment the sun sets
They keep on being consumed by the fire
From where do we know?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse מבוא השמש ('after sunset') with עם בא השמש ('with sunset'). The whole answer depends on this small change: the service is done by day, and only the burning goes on into the night.

phrases.english: Rather, [items put up] together with sunset,
which keep being consumed all through the night: from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading of the text (from 'after sunset' to 'with sunset')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows starting daytime items after sunset.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks about items put up at sunset that keep burning through the night.

steps.title: The source: 'זאת תורת העולה' includes them
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings its source. The פסוק 'זאת תורת העולה' includes everything offered on the מזבח, so these items may also burn all night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'This is the law of the עולה.' This includes them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the עולה says it burns on the מזבח all night. The word 'תורת' ('the law of') is read as including other things too. So all-night burning applies to these daytime items as well.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches,' introducing a source from a פסוק
The law of the עולה, the burnt offering
It included, meaning it widened the law to cover more cases

phrases.english: The verse states:
"This is the law of the burnt offering": it included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the question as reread in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: Daytime items put up at sunset may keep burning all night
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 6:2, 'זאת תורת העולה', read as including everything offered on the מזבח

steps.title: At sunset the fire cannot catch most of it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the קומץ is put up right at sunset, the fire cannot take hold of most of it while it is still day. That seems to clash with רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it is put up together with sunset, you cannot find that the fire takes hold of most of it [before night].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי יוחנן's rule from step 16 and asks how the ברייתא fits with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the fire must catch most of the קומץ. When the קומץ is put up at the last moment of day, most of it burns only at night. So the burning seems not to work, yet the ברייתא treats it as valid.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot find such a case
That the fire catches, takes hold of it
Most of it, the majority

phrases.english: But [if it is put up] together with sunset,

phrases.aramaic: לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ שֶׁתַּצִּית הָאוּר בְּרוּבּוֹ.
phrases.english: you cannot find that the fire catches most of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the reread ברייתא (step 21) against רבי יוחנן's rule (step 16).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule (step 16) that the fire must take hold of most of the קומץ, challenged from the ברייתא as reread in step 21
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats a קומץ put up at sunset as a valid burning, even though the fire cannot take hold of most of it while it is still day. That seems to contradict רבי יוחנן's requirement that most of it be burning.

steps.title: Two different stages: the מזבח taking hold vs. permitting the שיריים
steps.stepSummary: The answer: there is no conflict. The ברייתא only needs the מזבח to 'take hold' of the קומץ. רבי יוחנן's 'most of it' is needed to permit the שיריים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, the ברייתא is talking about the מזבח taking hold of it. There, רבי יוחנן is talking about permitting the שיריים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash by showing that the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן are talking about two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the קומץ to become the מזבח's food and keep burning all night, it is enough for the fire to start catching it. Permitting the כהנים to eat the שיריים is a separate result. Only that result needs the fire to catch most of it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, meaning there is no real contradiction
To 'take in.' The מזבח takes hold of the קומץ as its own
To permit, here meaning to let the כהנים eat the שיריים

steps.whatToRemember: The fire catching the קומץ has two separate results. A small catch is enough for the מזבח to 'take hold' (לקלוט). Only a catch of most of it permits the שיריים (להתיר), according to רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here it is for receiving, there it is for permitting.
phrases.notes: 'Receiving' means the מזבח takes the קומץ as its own. 'Permitting' means letting the כהנים eat what is left.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן לִקְלוֹט, כָּאן לְהַתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two different legal results (two cases)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources talk about the same result, so they conflict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks about the מזבח taking hold. רבי יוחנן speaks about permitting the שיריים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a single act, the fire catching the קומץ, can have more than one legal effect, and each effect can have its own requirement.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר keeps 'after sunset' and explains it as pieces that jumped off
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר keeps the ברייתא's original wording, 'after sunset.' He explains it as pieces that jumped off the fire, which may be put back during the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר teaches the ברייתא as 'after sunset,' and explains that it is talking about pieces that jumped off the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a different way to answer the question of step 20. It keeps the words 'after sunset' without changing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mean that the service starts at night. It means that pieces already burning, which fell off the fire, may be put back on after sunset. That is how 'after sunset' fits with 'items offered by day.'

keyTerms.meaning: He sets it in a specific case
Pieces that jumped or fell off the fire on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar teaches it "after sunset,"
and he sets it in the case of pieces that jumped off,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 20, instead of the reread in step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'After sunset' must mean starting the service at night, which cannot be.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'After sunset' refers to putting back pieces that jumped off the fire.

steps.title: רבי ינאי also says it is about pieces that jumped off
steps.stepSummary: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he reported that רבי ינאי also explained the ברייתא as talking about pieces that jumped off.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, when רב דימי came, he said that רבי ינאי said: it is about pieces that jumped off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support for רבי אלעזר's explanation from another sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי gives the same explanation. This shows that the 'pieces that jumped off' reading was not רבי אלעזר's alone. Nothing new is added; it only backs up step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly, bringing support for the same idea
When he came, usually meaning from ארץ ישראל to בבל

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to understand the ברייתא. One reads it as 'with sunset' (items put up by day that burn through the night). The other, from רבי אלעזר and רבי ינאי, keeps 'after sunset' and applies it to pieces that jumped off the fire.

phrases.english: And similarly, when Rav Dimi came,
[he said that] Rabbi Yannai said: it is about pieces that jumped off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's explanation from step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא refers to pieces that jumped off the fire
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ינאי's statement, reported by רב דימי

steps.title: Did רבי ינאי really say that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי ינאי could explain the ברייתא as pieces that jumped off, when he himself said that קטורת which jumped off may not be put back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי ינאי really say this? But רבי ינאי said: if קטורת jumped off the top of the מזבח, we do not put back even its small lumps!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the report from step 26. It says רבי ינאי contradicts himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists קטורת among the things that may burn all night. If רבי ינאי reads it as talking about pieces that jumped off, then jumped-off קטורת could be put back. But רבי ינאי elsewhere says jumped-off קטורת is never put back, not even tiny lumps.

keyTerms.meaning: Incense burned on the inner מזבח
Jumped off, popped off (from the fire)
Small lumps or crumbs
We put back (onto the fire)

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yannai really say this?
phrases.notes: "This" means his reading in step 26, that the ברייתא is about pieces that jumped off the fire, and that list included קטורת.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yannai say:
Incense that jumped off the top of the altar,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ קְרָטִין שֶׁבָּהּ אֵין מַחֲזִירִין אוֹתָן!
phrases.english: even its small lumps, we do not put them back!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the report in step 26 by pointing to a different statement of רבי ינאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's reading that the ברייתא, which includes קטורת, is about pieces that jumped off
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: רבי ינאי rules elsewhere that jumped-off קטורת is never put back.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up the challenge about קטורת
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns from a פסוק that partly burned pieces of an עולה are put back, but partly burned קטורת is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא בר מנייומי taught from the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: "That which the fire will consume of the עולה on the מזבח" teaches that you put back partly burned pieces of an עולה, but you do not put back partly burned קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its challenge with a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the עולה specifically. So only partly burned עולה pieces go back on the fire. קטורת is left out, which makes the problem with the ברייתא's list even sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: Partly burned ("partly eaten up") pieces
Burnt offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
From the school (study house) of

phrases.english: And Rav Chanina bar Minyumi taught
from the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכַל הָאֵשׁ אֶת הָעֹלָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״ –
phrases.english: "That which the fire will consume of the burnt offering on the altar":
partly burned pieces of a burnt offering you put back,
but you do not put back partly burned incense!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנֵי רַב חֲנִינָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי בִּדְבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that supports the challenge raised in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That jumped-off קטורת is not put back
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 6:3 as taught in the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: Take קטורת off the list
steps.stepSummary: The answer is to remove the word קטורת from the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Remove קטורת from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the ברייתא's wording. קטורת is taken out of its list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קטורת gone, the ברייתא no longer clashes with רבי ינאי or with the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The reading of "pieces that jumped off" can stay for everything else on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove (this word) from here

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is read as being about pieces that jumped off the fire, but קטורת is removed from its list, because jumped-off קטורת is never put back.

phrases.english: Remove incense from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 27 and 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the text: one item is removed from the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's list includes קטורת, so jumped-off קטורת would be put back
steps.terutzMaskana: קטורת is not on the list; only the other items are put back if they jump off

steps.title: A קומץ under the wood pile
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks: if the קומץ was placed first and the wood pile was arranged on top of it, is that a proper way to burn it? The question is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: when רבי אלעזר explained the laws of מנחות, he asked this. If the כהן placed the קומץ and then arranged the wood pile on top of it, what is the law? Is that a proper way of burning or not? It stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי אלעזר asks whether a קומץ placed under the wood, instead of on top of it, counts as properly burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the קומץ is placed on top of the burning wood. Here the order is flipped: the קומץ is underneath. The question is whether burning "the wrong way around" still counts. No answer is found, so it ends in תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of a מנחה that is burned on the מזבח
The arranged pile of wood on the מזבח
The proper way of burning an offering
"Let it stand": the question stays unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is "no." It means the גמרא could not decide either way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
When Rabbi Elazar would explain the laws of meal offerings,
he would ask this:
Rabbi Elazar asks:
A handful that he arranged on the altar,
and then he arranged the wood pile on top of it, what is the law?
Is this a proper way of burning,
or is this not a proper way of burning?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how an offering must be placed on the wood pile.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does burning a קומץ that lies underneath the wood count as proper burning?

steps.title: Limbs under the wood pile
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה asks the same question about the limbs of an עולה. The פסוק "על העצים" suggests they must be on the wood, but another פסוק says "על המזבח." The question is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה asks: if the כהן arranged the limbs and then arranged the wood pile on top of them, what is the law? Does "on the wood" mean only on the wood? Or, since another פסוק says "on the מזבח," may he do it either way? It stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה asks a question like רבי אלעזר's, but about the limbs of an עולה. He also gives the two sides of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says the limbs go "on the wood," which sounds like a strict requirement. A second פסוק says "on the מזבח," which sounds like any placement on the מזבח is fine. Since the two פסוקים point in different directions, the כהן may possibly choose either way. No answer is found.

keyTerms.meaning: The limbs (body parts) of an offering
"On the wood" (ויקרא 1:8)
Specifically, only this way

phrases.english: Chizkiya asks:
Limbs that he arranged on the altar
and then he arranged the wood pile on top of them, what is the law?
Does the Torah say "on the wood" to mean
specifically on the wood?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיב קְרָא אַחֲרִינָא:
phrases.english: Or perhaps, since another verse is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכַל הָאֵשׁ אֶת הָעֹלָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״,
phrases.english: "That which the fire will consume of the burnt offering on the altar,"
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק from step 28, ויקרא 6:3. Here the focus is on the words "on the מזבח."

Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question as step 30, this time about the limbs of an עולה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must the limbs be on top of the wood, or may they be under it?

steps.title: Limbs beside the wood pile
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא asks about limbs placed next to the wood pile, neither on top of it nor under it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא asks: if the כהן arranged the limbs beside the wood pile, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A third question about placement. This time the limbs sit at the side of the wood pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the limbs are neither on the wood nor under it. They are next to it. The גמרא will next explain which opinions this question applies to.

keyTerms.meaning: At the sides of, next to

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha asks:
Limbs that he arranged at the sides of the wood pile, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third placement case after steps 30 and 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is placing the limbs beside the wood pile acceptable?

steps.title: No question for the one who reads "on" literally
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to narrow down רבי יצחק נפחא's question. According to the view that "on" the wood means literally on top of it, there is no question.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says "on" means literally on top, you do not need to ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up where the question really applies. First it rules out one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "on the wood" means literally on top, then limbs placed beside the wood are clearly not on it, so the case is obvious. The question can only arise according to a less literal reading, which the גמרא is about to give.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: According to the one who says "on" means literally on top,
phrases.notes: "On" refers to the words "on the wood" from the פסוק in step 31.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר ״עַל״ מַמָּשׁ לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from step 32 by ruling out one opinion where it would not arise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the view that "on" means literally on top, limbs beside the wood are clearly not acceptable, so there is nothing to ask.
